cheng-gnn-review-five-years-scope: Section 3, p.4: the authors state the window and size of their own review. Verified in context.
cheng-gnn-four-types: Section 3, p.4: the paper states its own four-way categorization. The four names are in the headings of Sections 3.1 to 3.4, not in the quote.
cheng-gnn-message-passing-definition: Section 2.2, p.3-4: the paper defines message passing with Eqs. (1) and (2) and the two phases (aggregate, update).
cheng-gnn-application-areas: Section 6, p.10: the paper states which areas its application section covers.
cheng-review-scope: Abstract, p.1: the paper states over 100 studies reviewed. Section 3 repeats it.
cheng-darbo-definition: Section 1, p.2: the paper defines DARBO and its two adaptive regions in its own words.
cheng-approximation-ratio-definition: Section 2.1, p.6: the paper defines r and the gap 1-r for MAX-CUT.
cheng-w3r-graph-definition: Section 2.1, p.6: 'Throughout this work' states the one problem family studied.
cheng-hardware-setup-shots-trials: Figure 4 caption, p.7: 10000 shots, five trials per line, best success ratio of five. All in the caption.
cheng-hardware-20-qubit-5-qubit-setup: Figure 1 caption, p.3: 5-qubit program on a 20-qubit processor with error mitigation.
cheng-darbo-trust-region-settings: Section 4 Methods, p.12: Lmin, Lmax, tau_s and tau_f are stated as this study's settings.
cheng-darbo-search-region-settings: Section 4 Methods, p.12-13: kappa_s = 4 and beta = 0.2 are stated as this study's settings.
cheng-darbo-max-iterations: Section 4 Methods, p.11: maximum of 1000 iterations 'in this work'.
cheng-zne-settings: Section 4 Methods, p.14-15: error rates [1,3,5], linear for p=1 and quadratic for p=2, readout mitigation first. All stated for the main-text experiments.
cheng-darbo-low-dimension-limit: Section 3, p.10: the authors say the parameter dimension in this work is still relatively low and name larger-parameter variational algorithms as future work. The future-work half is in the passage after the quote.
cheng-hardware-proof-of-concept-scope: Section 1, p.3 and Section 3, p.10: the run is called a proof of concept on five qubits, and the paper says scaling with meaningful accuracy needs more pruning, compiling and mitigation. Both are limits the paper states about its own work.
rle-theorem-1-qubit-bound: Theorem 1, p.3 (checked on the page image: Q <= 2N log M). Proof in Appendix C, p.10-11, from Lemma 1 plus the Hamming and Gilbert-Varshamov bounds, which the proof adapts to the even-weight subspace. Proof is brief but in the paper.
rle-lemma-1-kernel-weight: Lemma 1, Appendix C, p.10 (checked on the page image). Proof follows in the paper: two distinct weight-N bitstrings that collide in the encoded space.
rle-theorem-2-measurement-bases: Theorem 2, p.3 and Appendix D, p.12. The proof counts distinct X-strings, C(M,0)+C(M,2)+C(M,4), using Lemmas 2 and 3. Proof is in the paper.
rle-lemma-2-xp-form: Lemma 2, Appendix D, p.11. Proof from the Jordan-Wigner form, Eqs. (D1) to (D6), is in the paper.
rle-lemma-3-one-basis: Lemma 3, Appendix D, p.11-12. Proof by the CNOT (Clifford) transformation, Eqs. (D7) to (D13), is in the paper.
rle-corollary-1-x-strings: Corollary 1, Appendix D, p.12. A short proof from the proof of Theorem 2 follows in the paper.
rle-proposition-1-quantum-decoder: Proposition 1, Section IV.C, p.4-5. Proof in the paper uses Bennett's theorem and the deferred measurement principle, both cited standard results, then Eqs. (8) to (10).
rle-proposition-2-multicontrolled: Proposition 2, Appendix E.1, p.12-13. Proof in the paper from Lemma 3 and exponentiation of commuting terms.
rle-parallelization-limit: Appendix D, p.12: inside the proof of Theorem 2 the authors state that maximal linear encoding breaks parallelization, so the bound is for no parallelization. A limit of their own scheme.
rle-vqe-setup-optimizer-averaging: Section V, p.6: L-BFGS-B, HEA, Hartree-Fock start, 30 averaged runs. Stated as the benchmark setup.
rle-vqe-system-sizes: Section V, p.6: LiH STO-3G M=8,N=2 to 6 qubits and H2 6-311G* M=12,N=2 to 7 qubits. Numerals read in the text layer; they agree with the Appendix tables.
rle-open-question-general-algorithms: Section VI, p.7: the authors name the use of the trade-offs for more general algorithms as an open question, so outside what the paper covers.
rle-hea-definition: Appendix H.2, p.16-17: the paper defines its HEA with the two gate types and a one-dimensional chain.
rle-qubit-gate-tradeoff: Appendix E.3, p.14: the authors state that the qubit reduction costs gate complexity. A cost of their own scheme. Appendix E.1 also gives a combinatorial worst case.
rle-fed-vqe-limit-ansatz: Appendix G, p.15: 'the demonstration is limited to non-physically motivated ansatze, and it remains unexplored whether the RLE-FED protocol can facilitate the scalable implementation of VQE'. A limit the paper states on its own results.
rle-fed-vqe-test-setup: Abstract, p.1: states the test systems and bases. Section V, p.6 and Appendix H give the same systems (LiH STO-3G and 6-31G, H2 6-311G*).
qhd-cd-modularity-definition: Section III.A, p.2: Eq. (1) and the text define modularity with A_ij, degrees and the Kronecker delta. Value matches.
qhd-cd-qubo-objective-terms: Section III.B, p.3: Eq. (5) and the sentence after it define the three terms.
qhd-cd-multilevel-refinement-classical: Section III.B.2, p.4: the paper defines initial partition by Eq. (5) and refinement by modularity gain, with the stop rule. Algorithm 2 shows the same.
qhd-cd-heavy-edge-coarsening: Section III.B.2, p.3-4: Eq. (6) defines the heavy-edge weight with alpha and beta.
qhd-cd-eval-machine: Section V.A, p.5: OS, kernel, CPU and RAM stated.
qhd-cd-time-parity-method: Section V.B, p.5: the time-parity protocol is stated. Section V.C also says QHD used 20% of GUROBI's time, which sits oddly with equal limits, but the value states only the method.
qhd-cd-small-networks-testbed: Section V.C, p.5: matches Table I (52 to 1,034 nodes, 146 to 26,749 edges, density 3.38 to 15.15 percent).
cheng-setup-quantum-inspired: Abstract p.1 and Section V.A-B, p.5: stated algorithm, four A5000 GPUs for QHD, GUROBI on CPUs, equal time limit. Section V.C reports QHD at 20% of GUROBI's time, in tension with equal limits; the value restates only the paper's stated protocol.
shim-tutorial-scope-automated-methods: Abstract, p.1: the tutorial states its examples, code and two automated methods.
shim-qa-definition-hamiltonians: Part I.A, p.3: Eqs. (1) to (3) and the text define QA, H(s), s, Gamma(s) and J(s).
shim-ideal-annealer-definition: Part I.B, p.3-4: 'An ideal annealer, in this work, is defined simply as...'. Text spans the Figure 1 break.
shim-core-principle-observables: Part I.C, p.4: the authors state the approach of the tutorial. The 'in experiment they can differ' part is part of the stated approach, not tested here.
shim-observables-scope-100-samples: Part I.C, p.4: only one- and two-spin observables, 100 samples per call for all examples. The text says 'in part because' they are easy to tune; the value drops 'in part', a small softening only.
shim-orbit-definition: Part I.C, p.5: orbits defined by the two properties 'guaranteed by symmetry in an ideal annealer'.
shim-orbits-not-unique: Part I.C, p.5: the paper states the non-uniqueness of orbits and why a separate-orbit choice is useless.
shim-signed-ising-construction: Part I.C.1, p.5: the construction is given step by step with the informal summary.
shim-automorphism-orbits-method: Part I.C.1, p.5 and footnote 2: orbits come from the automorphism group of S(h,J); nauty needs a vertex-labeled graph.
shim-fm-loop-setup: Part II, p.7 and II.B: L = 64, J = -0.2, 1 microsecond anneals, 100 samples per call.
shim-embedding-method-glasgow: Part II.A, p.7: Glasgow solver in minorminer, 2x2 raster scan of Pegasus unit cells, greedy disjoint set.
shim-fbo-vs-h-definition: Part II.B, p.7: h_i scales with J(s); the FBO is constant in s. The text says they prefer FBOs 'in part because' they are programmed independently of h_i; the value drops 'in part', a small softening only.
shim-fbo-update-rule: Part II.B, p.7: Eq. (6) and the sign rule define the gradient-descent update.
shim-coupler-update-rule-fig7-protocol: Part II.C, p.9: Eq. (8) uses the residual frustration; the 100/100/100 iteration protocol with alpha_J = 0.001 is stated.
shim-gauge-transformation-derivation: Part III.A, p.10: 'We can derive this fact as follows.' A short complete argument: a gauge flip leaves the frustration probability unchanged in an ideal annealer, the loop returns by a cyclic shift, so all couplers match. Relies on the paper's own definition of an ideal annealer. Informal in tone, but the whole argument is in the paper.
shim-tafm-setup: Part IV.A, p.13: 12x12 cylindrical lattice, 10 disjoint embeddings, J_AFM = 0.9, J_FM = -2 J_AFM, shim of AFM couplers only. The 'FM rarely frustrated' reason is the authors' stated rationale.
shim-fig13-setup: Figure 13 caption, p.14: 800 iterations, FBO shim after 100, coupler shim after 300.
shim-coupler-range-truncation: Part IV.C.1, p.15: range [-2, 1], 1.11 x J_AFM, renormalize to 0.9 before truncation.
shim-psi-definition: Part IV.C.3, p.16: psi defined from a 3-coloring in Eq. (9). The sixfold symmetry is stated as an expectation, which the value reports as such.
shim-adaptive-step-rule: Part IV.D, p.17: the four-step rule with lookback 20 and epsilon 0.1 is stated as given.
shim-damping-limit: Part VI.A-B, p.20: shimming can take many iterations; damping can undercompensate biases; damping is only recommended when the shim is badly behaved. Limits and advice the paper states about its own method.
chern-scope-advantage-processor: Part VII, p.21: the examples are written for an Advantage processor and the authors say they are not specific to it. The generality is the authors' statement of scope, not tested.
chern-shimming-definition: Part I.B, p.3: 'This is achieved by shimming: inferring statistical features of an ideal annealer, and tuning the Hamiltonian'.

theory_low.shim-fm-loop-ground-states: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Figure 2 caption, p.4. Ground-state degeneracy of the ferromagnetic and frustrated loops is a standard fact, stated without derivation; the h = 0 zero-magnetization remark is stated 'trivially'.
theory_low.shim-frustrated-loop-equal-frustration: Part III, p.10. Two parts: zero magnetization 'obvious... since there is no symmetry-breaking field' is stated, not shown (textbook, stated not proved (F129)). The equal-frustration part is derived in III.A (see shim-gauge-transformation-derivation). Graded by the weaker.
theory_low.shim-fig9-frustrated-loop-orbits: Figure 9 caption, p.10: an output of the paper's code on one example (three frustrated six-qubit loops), not a proof.
theory_low.shim-copies-share-orbits: Part III.A, p.11: textbook, stated not proved (F129). The paper calls it 'an obvious but useful fact'; it follows from the orbit definition but is not argued.
theory_low.shim-fig11-buckyball-orbits: Figure 11 caption, p.12: a computed result on one example (Buckyball); vertex-transitivity is a known graph fact stated without proof.

value_replace.shim-observables-scope-100-samples: The authors state that in this work they consider only one- and two-spin observables, and that they set the number of samples per QPU call to 100 for all examples.
value_replace.shim-fbo-vs-h-definition: The authors state that each qubit can be biased by a programmable longitudinal field hi, whose bias is scaled by J(s) and so changes with s, or by a programmable flux-bias offset, which confers a constant bias independent of s, and that they prefer flux-bias offsets to mitigate biases in part because they are programmed independently of hi.
